claims.title: Two-sided pathwise KT sandwich: ln BF_n = n KL(qhat || 1/2) - (1/2) ln n - c_n(x) with c_n(x) in ((1/2) ln(pi/2), ln 2] for every sequence
claims.scope: every n >= 1 and every binary sequence x of length n; BF_n is the Krichevsky-Trofimov (Jeffreys mixture) Bayes factor against fair bits
assumptions: BF_n(x) = 2^n P_KT(x) with P_KT the Beta(1/2,1/2) mixture of Bernoulli product laws
qhat is the empirical frequency of ones in x
nonclaims: the upper regret bound is the classical KT bound (Krichevsky-Trofimov 1981; Willems-Shtarkov-Tjalkens 1995) and is not claimed as new; only the uniform pathwise lower bound rho_n(x) > (1/2) ln(pi n/2) is claimed, and its gamma-function inequality is standard
two-sided pathwise KT and Jeffreys regret bounds appear in Freund 1996 and Xie-Barron 2000; no priority is claimed for the lower bound
the upper constant ln 2 is attained only at n = 1; the exact maximal regret for n >= 2 is not given
the sandwich concerns the KT composite alternative only, not other priors on the bias

claims.title: Non-asymptotic expected-evidence sandwich: n KL(q || 1/2) - (1/2) ln n - ln 2 <= E_q[ln BF_n] <= n KL(q || 1/2) - (1/2) ln n + 1 - (1/2) ln(pi/2)
claims.scope: IID Bernoulli(q) bits, every q in [0,1] and every n >= 1
assumptions: bits are IID Bernoulli(q) under the data-generating law
the test statistic is the KT Bayes factor of ST-T272
nonclaims: the lower half is ST-T271; only the expected upper bound is new
the sandwich is not tight to o(1); ST-T274 gives the limit
it says nothing about dependent, adaptive, or adversarial bit sources
it is not evidence for or against simulation; a simulator with q = 1/2 is invisible (ST-T01)

claims.title: Exact additive constant (Clarke-Barron, specialized): E_q[ln BF_n] = n KL(q || 1/2) - (1/2) ln n + (1/2) ln(2e/pi) + o(1) for interior q, and constant -(1/2) ln pi at q in {0, 1}
claims.scope: fixed q in [0,1] as n grows
assumptions: bits are IID Bernoulli(q)
q is fixed while n grows (pointwise, not uniform, in q)
nonclaims: not new: the interior constant (1/2) ln(2e/pi) is the Clarke-Barron (1990, 1994) expansion for Bernoulli with the Jeffreys prior (see also Xie-Barron 1997, 2000), and the boundary constant follows from Wallis; the self-contained proof is a re-derivation
the o(1) term is not uniform near q = 0 or q = 1
the rate of the o(1) term is not proved (see ST-O02)

claims.title: Bounded high-precision certificate of the KT remainder table and the beacon-scale fair expectation
claims.scope: q in {1/10, 1/5, 1/4, 1/3, 2/5, 1/2} and n up to 5000; q = 1/2 at n = 131072; the committed beacon pulses
assumptions: Decimal arithmetic at 60 digits with correctly rounded ln; comparisons asserted with margin 1e-30
binomial tails beyond |k - n/2| > 4000 at n = 131072 are bounded by Hoeffding and contribute below 1e-100
the 80-digit cross-check uses 80-digit working precision with the 60-digit constants
nonclaims: the table certifies finitely many (n, q) pairs only
the exact fair expectation -5.6175 at n = 131072 is a property of the KT statistic, not of the beacon data; the observed -6.0317 is one realization

claims.title: Pathwise KT rejection region and Hoeffding power frontier for biased Bernoulli simulators
claims.scope: n IID Bernoulli(q) bits, level alpha and target power 1 - beta
assumptions: the test rejects fairness when BF_n >= 1/alpha (level alpha by Ville's inequality under fair bits, as in ST-T08)
bits are IID Bernoulli(q) under the alternative
nonclaims: the closed-form frontier d_n + sqrt(ln(1/beta)/(2n)) is sufficient, not necessary; the exact KT frontier is smaller (ST-F54)
the power step is Hoeffding's inequality and the region uses binary Pinsker; both are standard
the frontier concerns IID biased simulators and says nothing about simulators that match the fair law

claims.title: Le Cam two-point converse (standard): no level-alpha test reaches power 1 - beta at |q - 1/2| below max{(1 - alpha - beta)/sqrt(2n), sqrt(ln(1/(2(alpha + beta)))/(4n))} over the branches whose condition holds
claims.scope: randomized tests on n IID bits
assumptions: alpha + beta < 1 for the Pinsker branch and alpha + beta < 1/2 for the Bretagnolle-Huber branch
the test observes at most n bits; a sequential test that stops by time n is covered
nonclaims: a direct application of the classical Le Cam two-point method with Pinsker and Bretagnolle-Huber (Le Cam 1973; Bretagnolle-Huber 1979; Tsybakov 2009, Lemma 2.6); not claimed as new
the converse constant is not optimal; the exact Neyman-Pearson frontier is larger (ST-F54)
tests that may observe more than n bits are not covered

claims.title: Beacon power frontier at n = 131072: fixed-n converse 0.00201 < optimal NP 0.00548 < exact KT 0.00867 < closed form 0.00991
assumptions: n and k are re-derived from the pinned NIST pulse file of ST-F52
powers are computed by Decimal recursion at 60 digits; bracketing powers differ from 0.95 by more than 1e-30
KT and NP power are monotone in |q - 1/2| (lemma in the derivation, checked exactly for small n), so grid bisection brackets the crossing
nonclaims: powers are for the fixed-n test BF_n >= 1/alpha; the ST-F52 sequential test rejects at least as often, so the KT frontier is conservative for it
the converse is of order 1/sqrt(n) and is off by a sqrt(ln n) factor from the KT frontier; it does not match it
the frontier describes which IID biased simulators the sample could have caught; it is not a randomness certification
simulators with |q - 1/2| below 0.00201 are not shown to exist or not to exist

claims.title: Binary symmetric coarsening rescales the power frontier and converse by 1/(1 - 2f) and moves boundary sources into the interior constant
claims.scope: a known binary symmetric channel with flip probability f in [0, 1/2) applied independently to every bit; extends ST-M83
assumptions: the channel acts independently on every bit and is known
the observer only sees channel outputs
nonclaims: the rate contraction KL(q_f || 1/2) <= KL(q || 1/2) is ST-M83; only the frontier rescaling and the constant shift are new
the result does not cover unknown or adversarial channels
at f = 1/2 nothing is detectable, which is ST-T01, not a new result

claims.title: Persistent cap: KL(P_a^Y || P_b^Y) <= KL(a || b) (data processing; finite only when a << b) for every transcript design (any length, stopping rule or label-independent adaptive policy), and <= N KL(a || b) for N world draws
claims.scope: one persistent latent world M with laws a and b, a common observation kernel, standard Borel spaces
assumptions: both hypotheses share the kernel P(Y | M) and the experimenter's policy does not depend on the hypothesis label
for the N-draw statement, any common kernel from (M_1..M_N) to Y; equality to the sum of per-unit KLs needs independent units
nonclaims: the inequality is the classical data-processing inequality for KL (Csiszar 1967; Cover-Thomas Thm 2.8.1; Polyanskiy-Wu 2024) and is not claimed as new; the contribution is its application to world-level mixing weights
the bound is vacuous (+inf) when a is not << b; the ST-T226 support condition remains necessary for any finite ceiling
the two sides are not infinite together: KL(a || b) = +inf is compatible with KL(P_a^Y || P_b^Y) = 0 (identical components)
the bound controls the a-expected log Bayes factor, not every transcript (that is ST-T226)
it does not limit evidence about which latent model is active

claims.title: Saturation identity: KL(a || b) - KL(P_a^Y || P_b^Y) = E_a[KL(a(. | Y) || b(. | Y))], and for finite M the gap is zero iff a_m/b_m is constant on every posterior support
claims.scope: the ST-T277 setting with KL(a || b) < infinity; the zero-gap characterization for finite M
assumptions: KL(a || b) < infinity
posteriors are regular conditional distributions of M given Y under a x K and b x K
nonclaims: the identity is the KL chain rule, and the zero-gap condition specializes the Kullback-Leibler (1951) sufficiency equality condition; only the finite-M ratio form is stated here
the converse direction (gap 0 implies M is a.s. a function of Y) is guaranteed when the ratios a_m / b_m are pairwise distinct on supp(b); it fails in general (counterexamples in ST-F55)
the identity does not say how fast the gap closes; see ST-T279

claims.title: Gap bound (R - 1) P_a(MAP error) plus an explicit support-mismatch term; hence the gap decays at least as fast as exp(-T min C + o(T)) over relevant pairs
claims.scope: finite latent set, a << b, conditionally IID transcripts for the decay corollary
assumptions: a << b (otherwise the cap is +inf and the gap is undefined)
R = max over m, m' in supp(a) of (a_m b_m') / (b_m a_m')
for the decay corollary, the component laws in every relevant pair are distinct
the Chernoff parameter s may be chosen separately for each pair
nonclaims: the multi-hypothesis MAP-error Chernoff exponent is classical (Chernoff 1952; Leang-Johnson 1997); only the (R - 1) factor and the support-mismatch term are new
the decay rate is an upper bound on the gap's exponent, not shown to be tight
without distinct component laws the gap can stay bounded away from zero (non-identifying example in ST-F55)

claims.title: Component-kernel decomposition (standard): KL(P_a^Y || P_b^Y) <= KL(a || b) + E_a[KL(P^a_{Y|M} || P^b_{Y|M})]
claims.scope: hypotheses that differ in the mixing law and in the per-world kernels
assumptions: standard Borel spaces; kernels P^a_{Y|M}, P^b_{Y|M} measurable in M
the identity for the difference needs KL(a || b) + E_a KL(K^a || K^b) < infinity
nonclaims: chain rule plus data processing; standard and not claimed as new
no matching lower bound is claimed in general
it complements, and does not close, the ST-T226 scope nonclaim about component distinguishability
linear growth of the within-component part is evidence about per-world laws, not about the world-level weights

claims.title: Bounded exact-law audit of persistent-latent evidence, including counterexamples to the original sketch
claims.scope: binary, ternary, support-mismatch, ternary-emission and non-identifying examples up to T = 64; two counterexamples to 'gap 0 only if M is a function of Y'; one infinite-cap counterexample
assumptions: probabilities are exact Fractions over sufficient count vectors; logarithms are 60-digit Decimals with margin 1e-30
nonclaims: the reported value at T = 4 is 0.1794, not 0.180 as in the sketch
bounded examples do not validate any prior over simulators

claims.title: Second-order KT remainder: is r_n(q) = (1 - 2q)^2 / (24 n q (1 - q)) + O(1/n^2) for interior q?
claims.scope: r_n(q) is the ST-T274 remainder for fixed interior q
assumptions: formally derived by second-order moment and Stirling expansions; numerics agree
nonclaims: heuristically derived by second-order moment and Stirling expansions; numerics agree; the remainder control is not written, so it is not a theorem
at q = 1/2 the remainder 9.7e-12 at n = 131072 suggests O(1/n^2), also unproved
